summary.summary: PARTIAL on the backward cone of the 2+1 sphere law: the Polya-urn unit flow (uniform on every level, step probability (n_j+1)/(m+3)) has level energy exactly 1/((m+1)(m+3)), proved in closed form, so its total energy telescopes to E_T = 3/4 - (1/2)(1/(T+1) + 1/(T+2)) < 3/4 for every T; by Thomson's principle the cone's effective resistance is R_T <= E_T < 3/4 and its conductance - which is the minimum order-beta cost of a space-time twist reaching theta_0 at the apex, per theta_0^2 - satisfies C_T > 4/3 uniformly in T, confirmed against exact layer-elimination values C_1..C_5 = 3, 9/4, 117/59, 2595/1408, ... that reproduce attempt a4's table; the uniform-splitting flow, by contrast, has energy (1/3) sum_{m<T} P_m which diverges like log T, so 1/sum_k P_k is the reciprocal of a divergent upper bound on R_T - a lower bound on the conductance that tends to 0

review: Both prior attempts on this problem are mine, so I did not re-run either route. I took the task's GIVEN (2) - that the minimum space-time twist cost is exactly 1/sum_k P_k and tends to zero - and tested it against the object a1 and a4 had already put on the table, since GIVEN (2), a4's extrapolated limit 1.38 and a1's bounded flow cannot all be true. The Polya-urn flow's level energy has the closed form 1/((m+1)(m+3)), which telescopes to E_T = 3/4 - (1/2)(1/(T+1)+1/(T+2)) < 3/4, so Thomson gives C_T > 4/3 uniformly and GIVEN (2) is false: 1/sum_k P_k is the reciprocal of a divergent upper bound on the resistance, a lower bound on the conductance read as its value. I recomputed the conductance independently by exact layer elimination and it reproduces a4's table at T = 1..5, confirming a4's numbers while replacing its extrapolation with a proof and sharpening a1's bound by a factor 2.6. I caught one inverted inequality in my own assertion (Thomson gives C_T E_T >= 1, not <=) before the final run. The task's actual target, m_t -> 0, is NOT proved: only Route A is closed, and Route B is now the only live route.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: Memory loss of the sphere law in 2+1, with the referee's two openings. GIVEN (referee reports on four failed attempts): (1) the linear model DOES forget in the relevant sense: on the plane the transverse variance of a site grows like (3 sqrt 3/(4 pi)) sigma^2 log t (exact return sums), so the magnetization of the Gaussian approximation decays like a power; the conserved quantity is only the mean of the zero mode. (2) The twist route is alive: for a space-TIME twist field theta(x,t) the order-beta cost has minimum exactly 1/sum_{k<T} P_k, which tends to 0 by recurrence of the plane walk; attempts that used a twist static in level time found a cost Theta(T) and wrongly closed the route. (3) KL(vMF(k u) || vMF(k u')) = k A(k)(1 - u.u') exactly. TASK: prove m_t -> 0 on the infinite plane for every beta (block 26's open statement, PR #8170). Route A: the space-time twist: construct theta(x,t) = theta_0 g_T(x,t) with g built from the walk's Green function truncated at T, bound the path-space relative entropy by C beta theta_0^2/sum_{k<T}P_k, and conclude by the entropy inequality that the law of the record at the origin at level T is nearly invariant under rotation by theta_0. Route B: a lower bound on the growth of the transverse variance of the nonlinear law by comparison with the linear one. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<name>/check.py"
